query: For steels used in chemical-processing and nuclear-power applications, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain their resistance to corrosion? Specify a controlled study capable of revealing the governing cause, predicted observations relative to a baseline, the boundaries within which the hypothesis should hold, supporting evidence from prior findings, and a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The corrosion resistance of steels used in chemical-processing and nuclear-power applications is primarily governed by the formation of a dense Cr2O3 passivation film on the surface, which acts as a barrier to prevent the penetration of corrosive species.
generation.material_initial_state: Uncorroded steel with a chromium content of at least 10%
generation.intervention: Exposure to a corrosive environment with a temperature range of 20-100°C and a humidity level of 40-80%
generation.conditions: The steel is subjected to a controlled environment with a constant flow of corrosive species
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of a dense Cr2O3 passivation film on the surface of the steel
generation.mechanism: The Cr2O3 passivation film acts as a barrier to prevent the penetration of corrosive species, thereby reducing the corrosion rate
generation.predicted_outcome: A reduction in corrosion rate of at least 50% compared to a steel without a Cr2O3 passivation film
generation.baseline: A steel without a Cr2O3 passivation film
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is valid for steels with a chromium content of at least 10% and exposed to a corrosive environment with a temperature range of 20-100°C and a humidity level of 40-80%
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanism of corrosion resistance is not fully understood and may involve other factors such as the presence of other alloying elements or the formation of other oxide layers

falsification_experiment.design: A controlled experiment where steels with different chromium contents are exposed to a corrosive environment and the corrosion rate is measured
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the corrosion rate of steels with a chromium content of at least 10% is not significantly lower than that of steels without a Cr2O3 passivation film, then the hypothesis is falsified. A significant difference is defined as a reduction in corrosion rate of at least 50%.

cited_evidence.text: Early research reported that stainless steel, Fe-Cr alloy, and CrFe15Ni15 alloy have excellent corrosion resistance due to the dense Cr2O3 passivation film formed on the surface [,,]. Similarly, it was speculated that the Cr2O3 passivation film has the same effect in the corrosion resistance of HEAs. AlCoCrFeNi [], AlxCrFe1.5MnNi0.5 [], and Al0.5CoCrCuFeNiBx [] verified the foregoing speculation. Therefore, for the (CoCrFeNi)95Nb5 HEA coating passivation film of this study, it can be obtained from the results of XPS that the Cr2O3 in the passivation film provides good corrosion resistance for the coating, and the addition of trace amount of Nb results in forming a stable metal oxide of Nb2O5 in the passivation film of the coating, which also plays a positive role in the corrosion resistance [,].

Severe plastic deformation (SPD) techniques enable the fabrication of ultrafine-grained (UFG) or nanocrystalline (NC) materials in bulk forms suitable for load-carrying structural applications []. With the advent of SPD, there has been an increasing demand to clarify the effect of UFG/NC formation on corrosion from a practical viewpoint, especially with regard to the classic topic of the effect of grain size on corrosion [,]. Among the various materials investigated to date, stainless steels exhibited mostly improved corrosion resistance by forming UFG structures by SPD [,,,,,,,]. The enhanced corrosion resistance of UFG/NC SSs compared with coarse-grained (CG) materials has been mostly attributed to greater Cr enrichment in the passivation film [,,,,,,,,], which has been validated experimentally by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) [] and recently by Cs-corrected scanning-transmission electron microscopy (STEM) [,]. Two possibilities for the enhanced Cr enrichment in the passivation film of UFG/NC materials have been proposed.
